Bengal is the low, wet delta of the Ganges and Brahmaputra rivers in the east of the Indian subcontinent, now split between Bangladesh and India. The map shows it from 1492 to 1600, when it was a rich sultanate and then a Mughal province, and again in 1783 under British rule.

In 1352 Ilyas Shah united the region as the independent Bengal Sultanate. It grew rice, silk and fine cotton cloth, and its ports traded across the Bay of Bengal. Under Husain Shah, who ruled from 1494 to 1519, the saint Chaitanya spread a new devotional worship of Krishna. Sher Shah Suri seized Bengal in 1538, and in 1576 the armies of Akbar made it part of the Mughal Empire.

After the Battle of Plassey in 1757 the East India Company took over its revenue. The famine of 1770 followed. By 1783 Calcutta was the capital of British India.
